hook: The park built for London's 2012 Olympic Games sits on land that was once rail yards, factories and dumps along the River Lea, with soil so polluted it had to be washed before anything could be built. Meanwhile, in Jakarta, parts of the city sink every year as wells pump water from under it. Cities are where most people will live, and where many of the world's environmental problems are made and must be solved.

options: Meeting people's needs without using up what future generations will need
Growing a city as fast as possible
Keeping a city's population the same forever
prereq.why: Sustainability balances present needs with the needs of the future.

prereq.q: What is an urban growth boundary?
options: A line beyond which building is limited
prereq.why: It steers building inside the line and protects rural land outside it.

options: Building on vacant or underused lots inside the built-up area
Clearing a neighborhood for a highway
prereq.why: Infill reuses land already inside the city.

figure.caption: An invented metro area with an urban growth boundary: an empty lot inside (X), farmland outside (Y), an old factory site (Z) and a rail station (W).

chain.cause: A city spreads over farmland at low density
chain.effect: people drive farther, so fuel use, air pollution and greenhouse gases rise

chain.cause: Paved surfaces replace fields and forest
chain.effect: rain runs off fast, carrying oil and trash into rivers and raising flood risk

chain.cause: Growth outpaces sewers and water pipes
chain.effect: untreated waste reaches water supplies, harming health

chain.cause: Cities clean up brownfields, protect farmland and plan across the whole region
chain.effect: growth goes onto land already in use, and the city's footprint on the land grows more slowly

ideas: Urban sustainability challenges include sprawl, sanitation, climate change, air and water quality, and energy use.
A city's ecological footprint is the area of land and water needed to supply what its people use and to absorb their waste. Cities' footprints are far larger than their own area.
A brownfield is an abandoned or underused industrial or commercial site that may be polluted. Cleaning it up lets the city grow inward instead of outward.
Responses include regional planning across many local governments, brownfield cleanup, urban growth boundaries and farmland protection. Each has costs as well as benefits.

misconception.wrong: A city's environmental impact stops at its city limits.
misconception.right: A city draws food, water, energy and materials from far away and sends its waste and emissions far away too. That is why its ecological footprint covers an area many times larger than the city itself.

summary: Growing cities face sprawl, poor sanitation, air and water pollution, high energy use and climate risks such as heat and flooding. Their ecological footprints reach far beyond their limits. Cities respond by cleaning up and reusing brownfields, drawing growth boundaries, protecting farmland and planning at the regional scale, and each response has trade-offs.
